facts.statement: Pterosaur fossils were first unearthed in 2009 in the Sebeș Formation near Lancrăm by paleontologist Mátyás Vremir.
facts.quote: Starting in 2009, pterosaur fossil remains were unearthed in a layer of the Sebeș Formation in Lancrăm, southwestern Transylvania by paleontologist Mátyás Vremir.

facts.statement: The genus and type species Eurazhdarcho langendorfensis were named in 2013 by Mátyás Vremir, Alexander Kellner, Darren Naish, and Gareth Dyke.
facts.quote: In 2013, he, along with paleontologists Alexander Kellner, Darren Naish, and Gareth Dyke would name the new genus and type species Eurazhdarcho langendorfensis.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is a partial skeleton containing neck vertebrae, metacarpals, and phalanx fragments.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Eurazhdarcho consists of a partial skeleton that includes cervical (neck) vertebrae, metacarpal, and phalanx fragments.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as EME VP 312, dates to the upper Early Maastrichtian, approximately 69 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, EME VP 312, was found in a layer of the Sebeș Formation dating from the upper Early Maastrichtian, about 69 million years old.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton is incomplete and lacks the skull.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull.

facts.statement: Comparisons with Zhejiangopterus suggest Eurazhdarcho had a wingspan of no more than 3 meters.
facts.quote: With extrapolations from the comparisons of cervical vertebrae and wingbones of Eurazhdarcho with those of the related azhdarchid Zhejiangopterus from China, Vremir and colleagues would estimate a wingspan not surpassing 3 m.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Eurazhdarcho likely hunted small terrestrial prey on land rather than eating fish, based on the abundance of land animals in its habitat.
facts.quote: Due to the abundance of terrestrial fauna in the Sebeș Formation, it has been suggested that Eurazhdarcho most likely fed by snatching small terrestrial prey while walking on all fours instead of being a fish-eater on the coast.

facts.statement: Evidence of scavenging includes circular bite marks on the fossil inflicted by a crocodyliform.
facts.quote: Afterwards it was exposed to the air, weathering and being scavenged as proven by circular bite-marks inflicted by the conical teeth of some member of the Crocodyliformes.

facts.statement: The third cervical vertebra is unusually long, reaching three-quarters the length of the fourth vertebra, compared to the normal 60 percent in azhdarchids.
facts.quote: The third neck vertebra has three-quarters of the length of the fourth vertebra, whereas 60 percent would be normal with azhdarchids.

facts.statement: A 2021 phylogenetic analysis by Brian Andres placed Eurazhdarcho in the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae.
facts.quote: In his 2021 study of Quetzalcoatlus, American paleontologist Brian Andres included Eurazhdarcho in his phylogenetic analysis. He placed Eurazhdarcho in the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae within Azhdarchidae.

facts.statement: A 2023 study by Rubi Pêgas and colleagues recovered Eurazhdarcho in a basal position within Azhdarchidae, clading it with Phosphatodraco, Wellnhopterus, and Aralazhdarcho.
facts.quote: In 2023, paleontologist Rubi Pêgas and colleagues recovered Eurazhdarcho in a different position within Azhdarchidae. They found it forming a clade with azhdarchids Phosphatodraco, Wellnhopterus, and Aralazhdarcho in a basal (primitive) position within the family.

facts.statement: The phylogenetic position of Eurazhdarcho within Azhdarchidae is debated, with studies placing it either in the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae or in a basal position.
facts.quote: Within Azhdarchidae, the position of Eurazhdarcho has been somewhat disputed, with some studies recovering it within the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae, while others have found it in a basal (primitive) position within the family.

facts.statement: The presence of terrestrial fauna supports the "superstork" model, suggesting Eurazhdarcho was a terrestrial stalker that snatched prey while walking on all fours.
facts.quote: This terrestrial fauna suggests that Eurazdarcho was not a coastal piscivore catching fish on the wing, affirming the "superstork" model for azhdarchids, in which they are terrestrial stalkers snatching small prey animals while walking on all fours.

facts.statement: The discovery implies two distinct azhdarchid species lived in the Hațeg fauna: the gigantic Hatzegopteryx and the medium-sized Eurazhdarcho.
facts.quote: If Eurazhdarcho was indeed distinct from Hatzegopteryx, its discovery implies the presence of two azhdarchid forms in the Hațeg fauna, the one gigantic, the other medium-sized.

facts.statement: Eurazhdarcho is an extinct genus of pterosaur belonging to the azhdarchid family, found in Transylvania, Romania, in Upper Cretaceous deposits.
facts.quote: Eurazhdarcho es un género extinto de pterosaurio perteneciente a la familia de los azdárquidos encontrado en la zona de Transilvania, Rumania, en depósitos del Cretácico Superior.

facts.statement: In 2009, Mátyás Vremir discovered pterosaur remains in Lancrǎm, near Sebeş-Glod in Transylvania, at site SbG-B.
facts.quote: En 2009, Mátyás Vremir descubrió los restos de un pterosaurio en Lancrǎm, cerca de Sebeş-Glod en Transilvania, en el sitio SbG-B.

facts.statement: In 2013, Vremir, Kellner, Naish, and Dyke named and described the type species Eurazhdarcho langendorfensis.
facts.quote: En 2013, Vremir, Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner, Darren Naish y Gareth Dyke nombraron y describieron a la especie tipo Eurazhdarcho langendorfensis.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton that lacks a skull.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial que carece del cráneo.

facts.statement: The holotype includes three cervical vertebrae (the third and fourth nearly complete), the third and fourth metacarpals, parts of wing finger phalanges, and some indeterminate fragments.
facts.quote: Incluye tres vértebras del cuello de entre las cuales la tercera y cuarta están casi completas; el tercer y cuarto metacarpiano; la parte superior de la primera falange del dedo alar; la parte inferior de la segunda falange; una falange inferior de uno de los otros dedos y algunos fragmentos indeterminados.

facts.statement: The carcass was likely deposited by a flood on its back in mud near a riverbank.
facts.quote: Probablemente el cadáver fue depositado por una inundación sobre su espalda en el fango cerca de la orilla de un río.

facts.statement: The fossil was later covered by a thin layer of mud and damaged by beetles and termites.
facts.quote: Más tarde fue cubierto por una delgada capa de lodo, siendo dañado por escarabajos y termitas

facts.statement: Evidence of circular bite marks inflicted by conical teeth of some Crocodyliform species suggests the carcass was scavenged.
facts.quote: como queda evidenciado por algunas marcas de mordidas circulares infligidas por los dientes cónicos de alguna especie de Crocodyliformes.

facts.statement: The third cervical vertebra was three-quarters the length of the fourth, whereas 60% is normal for azhdarchids.
facts.quote: La tercera vértebra del cuello tenía una longitud equivalente a tres cuartos de la longitud de la cuarta vértebra, mientras que el 60% de esa longitud es lo normal en los azdárquidos.

facts.statement: The prezygapophyses are well-developed and elongated, pointing obliquely forward and outward at a 30° angle relative to the vertebral axis.
facts.quote: Los cuellos de las prezigapófisis, el proceso de articulación frontal, están bien desarrollados y alargados, apuntando hacia adelante de forma oblicua y hacia afuera en un ángulo de 30° con respecto al largo eje de la vértebra.

facts.statement: Eurazhdarcho was assigned to the family Azhdarchidae based on comparative anatomy, without a cladistic analysis.
facts.quote: Eurazhdarcho fue asignado por los autores a la familia Azhdarchidae, basándose en el método de la anatomía comparada; no se llevó a cabo un análisis cladístico.

facts.statement: Eurazhdarcho was found in the Upper Cretaceous on the Hateg Island, part of the ancient European archipelago.
facts.quote: El área en la que se halló a Eurazhdarcho estaba localizada en el Cretácico Superior en la llamada Isla de Hațeg, parte del antiguo archipiélago europeo.

facts.statement: The terrestrial fauna suggests Eurazhdarcho was not a coastal piscivore, supporting the "super-stork" ecological model where azhdarchids were terrestrial predators capturing small animals while walking on four legs.
facts.quote: Esta fauna terrestre sugiere que Eurazdarcho no era un piscívoro costero que atrapaba peces volando, reafirmando el modelo ecológico de "supercigüeñas" de los azdárquidos, según el cual estos eran depredadores terrestres que capturaban animales pequeños mientras caminaban sobre sus cuatro patas.

facts.statement: It is unclear how the coexistence of large and medium azhdarchids correlates with specific prey preferences or hunting techniques.
facts.quote: aún no es claro como esto se correlaciona con la preferencia de determinadas presas o las técnicas de caza.

facts.statement: Eurazhdarcho lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Eurazhdarcho lived in what is now Romania about 69 million years ago during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: Eurazhdarcho is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur that lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Romania, about 69 million years ago.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'in what is now Romania about 69 million'

rejected.quote: El holotipo, EME VP 312, fue hallado en una capa de la Formación Sebeş que data de finales del Maastrichtiense Superior, hace cerca de sesenta y nueve millones de años.

rejected.statement: Eurazhdarcho is a medium-sized azhdarchid with an estimated wingspan of three meters, extrapolated from a fourth metacarpal length of about 25 centimeters.
rejected.quote: Eurazhdarcho es un azdárquido de tamaño medio. Los autores estimaron su envergadura en tres metros, extrapolándola de la longitud estimada del cuarto metacarpo de cerca de veinticinco centímetros.
